summary: The hooks actually run, and the panel holding your keyboard says so.
changes: Claude Code's hooks work from an installed copy. The application lives at `/Applications/Beacon Split.app`, and the space in that path meant the shell Claude runs hooks through read the command as ending at `/Applications/Beacon`, so every hook failed.

Installing the hooks twice no longer leaves two of them behind. Beacon looked for its own entries by product name, which appears in a development checkout's path and never in an installed build's, so each install added a copy rather than replacing one. Reinstalling from this version clears the duplicates.

Beacon finds the `claude` binary when it was started from the Dock. It asked an interactive shell where the binary lived, which a prompt theme or a git status daemon can wedge forever; the probe now gives up after four seconds and falls back to where the installers actually write.
The panel your keyboard is in is edged in the workspace colour, and ⌥⌘← / ⌥⌘→ move between panels.
The session panel no longer draws a slab of accent colour over its own contents.

summary: The first build worth handing to somebody else.
changes: Workspaces group projects, each with its own colour and icon, so you know where you are before reading anything.
A real claude session and a real shell per project, in their own PTYs. Beacon runs the CLI you already use rather than reimplementing it.
Sessions outlive the window: close Beacon and they keep running, open it again and it reattaches to them.
Layouts are a tree of splits with four presets, and every divider is draggable.
A file tree with an editor, a .env view that keeps values hidden until asked, and git status, diff, stage and commit.
Command palette on ⌘K, quick open on ⌘P, and every shortcut is editable.
Tabs say what Claude is doing — working, finished, or waiting for you — reported by Claude Code rather than guessed from output.
The title bar shows how much of the five-hour allowance is left and how full each project's context is.
Light and dark themes, how much of the desktop shows through the window, and whether what shows through is frosted.
